A1.justification: Both PDFs describe G-adaptivity for finite-element mesh relocation. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision and a changed title.

before.justification: V1 reports original Poisson and Burgers experiments, including FEM-error and mesh-generation timing results in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: V2 reports original Poisson, Burgers and Navier–Stokes experiments, including error reduction, relocation time and mesh-quality results in Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: V1's GRAND architecture with an identity encoder becomes a Diffformer using a learned Hessian-based encoder, separate latent-feature updates and blockwise positional diffusion. V2 also adds an equidistribution regularizer to the FEM objective and adopts Firedrake adjoint gradients with a reference-solution correction (Sections 4.1–4.4). These are procedural changes beyond renaming.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates one- and two-dimensional Poisson problems and one-dimensional Burgers dynamics on intervals and squares. V2 retains square Poisson coverage, removes the one-dimensional benchmarks, and adds polygonal Poisson domains, two-dimensional Burgers dynamics and Navier–Stokes flow around a cylinder in a multiply connected domain.

E2.justification: V1's MMPDE5 and M2N-inspired GAT/GAT_lap comparisons disappear. V2 evaluates UM2N and its regularized-PDE-loss variant UM2N-G, retains MA for Poisson and Burgers, and adds a measured DirectOpt comparison in Figure 1. Table 3 explicitly provides no MA performance result for Navier–Stokes.

E3.justification: V1 reuses training data for structured Poisson tests; v2 specifies held-out testing throughout, revised mesh resolutions and longer G-Adapt training, from 50 to 300 epochs. V2 adds aspect ratio, changes reference-solution projection and defines the error objective as squared L2 error. Burgers changes from semi-implicit 0.05 steps with remeshing every step to backward-Euler 0.02 steps with two-step rollout blocks and a separate ten-step experiment.

E4.justification: Architecture and training comparisons remain, but the Mesh-Loss/difFEM comparisons on G-adaptive and GAT variants become UM2N/UM2N-G/Diffformer comparisons. V2 adds a targeted ten-step Burgers experiment investigating optimization for less frequent remeshing and an illustrative comparison against direct mesh optimization in Figure 1.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without seed counts or uncertainty reporting. V2 specifies five random training seeds and reports plus/minus values for error reduction and aspect ratio throughout Tables 1–3. This introduces uncertainty reporting across the main evaluations, although the PDFs do not establish an increase from a known earlier run count, and v2 does not identify the error-bar statistic.

E6.justification: The principal results are replaced and expanded. V1's randg_275 comparison reports G-adaptive at -14.77% and MA at -13.84%; v2's square Poisson comparison reports 21.01 ± 0.33% and 12.69%, respectively. V2 also adds polygonal, two-dimensional Burgers and Navier–Stokes results, including 26.36 ± 1.37% for G-Adapt on Navier–Stokes. Changed settings and opposite error-reduction sign conventions prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: V1's Appendix C provides a one-dimensional continuous non-crossing proposition. V2 introduces Jacobian-based definitions, continuous and discrete preservation arguments, and explicit timestep bounds in Theorem 4.2 and Appendix F. It also adds a reference-gradient correction and formal regularized loss, while removing v1's detailed difFEM basis-function differentiation derivation.

C1.justification: Direct FEM-error optimization remains central, but v2 adds the equidistribution regularizer as a contribution and replaces the claimed new difFEM solver with training built on Firedrake. The conclusion changes from outperforming prior ML in both error and computational cost to lower error at similar cost. Multiply connected domains move from proposed future applicability to demonstrated coverage.

C2.justification: V2 attributes UM2N rollout failures to distribution shift and G-Adapt's resilience to structural regularization. It adds explanations of the regularizer's global guidance, interpolation costs motivating less frequent remeshing, and MA's difficulties on multiply connected domains. V1's explicit limitations concerning small meshes, weaker advantages at larger sizes and scalability are removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds block-integration settings, Hessian recovery, Gaussian-basis expansion details, Navier–Stokes discretizations and solver settings, and the dataset-resolution summary in Table 4. It replaces the custom difFEM implementation account with Firedrake integration details. Conversely, v1's M2 MacBook CPU disclosure, explicit Gaussian sampling ranges and repository link disappear; v2 only promises future code release.

R1.justification: V2 positions the architecture directly against UM2N and explicitly adopts its encoder and attention components. The solver-related contribution is repositioned around established Firedrake/pyadjoint capabilities, supported by new references on automated shape differentiation, adjoints and Hessian recovery. The broader distinction between direct FEM-error optimization and surrogate meshing remains.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, methodology and conclusion, moves GNN background into the method discussion, and reorganizes the appendices around implementation, Firedrake, PDE formulations, experiments and theory. The title and author list also change. The restructuring extends well beyond additions of scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, replaces the pipeline illustration with a new architecture flowchart, and introduces DirectOpt, polygonal, Burgers and cylinder-flow visualizations. Results tables are redesigned to include mesh quality and uncertainty, and Table 4 summarizes settings. The convex-hull illustration is retained as Figure 3, while appendix example montages are replaced.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical support through held-out testing, five-seed reporting, mesh-quality measurements and broader PDE/domain coverage. However, its expanded non-tangling argument in Appendix F assumes unestablished Laplacian symmetry and does not justify transferring the global graph-update determinant to individual element Jacobians; v1 supplied only a one-dimensional proposition. Removing the code link, hardware information and explicit scalability limitations also reduces transparency. These material gains and weaknesses leave the overall net quality change uncertain.
